body: Interesting, I didn't notice the closest point check was intentionally changed.  To support larger grab radiuses, I think the closest point logic in this PR is needed for cases where the points themselves are not overlapping but the grab areas are.  For when the points are overlapping, should it be easier to select the front point (using `break`), or easier to select the closest to the mouse (this PR's behavior)?  If we want to keep it easier to select the front point for overlaps, I could change this PR to still use the grab area to determine the closest, but break if under 8 (representing the point size).  I think editing the polygon in the 2D editor area chooses the closest point instead of front for overlaps, while the polygon panel editor chooses front on `master`.

> For when the points are overlapping, should it be easier to select the front point

This is more intuitive I think, though it's mostly a problem until #107890 is merged.

> I could change this PR to still use the grab area to determine the closest, but break if under 8

That could work.

I updated the `ACTION_REMOVE_INTERNAL` and `ACTION_ADD_POLYGON` cases to stop once a point is found within 8 pixels of the mouse position, similar to their current behavior on `master`.  I also updated `ACTION_EDIT_POINT` to stop in this case - this is new behavior compared to `master`, but I think it makes sense to keep the three cases consistent.  All three actions should now prioritize the front point when two or more points overlap.
